plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-SIWC

Sign in with ChatGPT on deepseek harness

The current package is `@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`, published on npm under the `alpha` dist-tag, with source and setup guidance in [`packages/chatgpt`](packages/chatgpt/README.md). The preserved v5 artifact under the former identity `@f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt@0.1.0` is historical only. This repository has no build-time dependency on a sibling DeepSeek Harness checkout.

The package declares compatibility with the DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1` through `0.2.1-alpha.4`, and `0.2.1-rc.2` API lines and their corresponding Cordis runtimes. Its build uses the published Typert generator with the narrow pinned patch in [`patches`](patches); the package tests check the generated Host Remote contract and OAuth lifecycle, while `pnpm run build` also builds the lazy Client entry point.

Run `pnpm install`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm test` from this directory. Profile requirements, account setup, headless browser sign-in, and model configuration are in the [package README](packages/chatgpt/README.md). Release operators can follow the [npm publishing guide](PUBLISHING.md).

## Install from npm

Install the published prerelease into an initialized Desktop profile with Desktop's managed `dsh` command (fully quit Desktop first):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5
```

The published `0.1.0-alpha.4` does not accept DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` in its compatibility range, so use `0.1.0-alpha.5` for the current DSH line. Use Desktop's bundled CLI or Plugin Manager, not an npm-installed `dsh` command. If the profile has the former package installed, fully quit Desktop and remove it before installing the renamed package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt
```

Do not keep both package names in one profile. The historical v5 artifact is [`@f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt@0.1.0`](dist/f4ah6o-dsh-chatgpt-0.1.0.tgz), SHA-256 `66ed59d58fe7d241d2cfcfc777939a7a3d7d49710cdce4cbecc9dcee8ffeeb2d`; it is an ignored, untracked workspace file. The prior prepublication `0.1.0` candidate is [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0.tgz), SHA-256 `15c16502dc658f752c5551b116d98dae286f32c69de3cc9e4d54a279ef1c4110`; its official and fork consumer matrix passed for that exact tarball. The published `0.1.0-alpha.5` artifact is [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@f12o/dsh-siwc/v/0.1.0-alpha.5), registry SHA-256 `9ca8b408d0336423aa02f25a1bdf8df39e67678d6b0dbc7bc153d2152dba3c55`, SHA-1 `f16d3aa8adae1e67183fbbb26d0a4f99b5fce1e2`, integrity `sha512-hlmoJgvXyIKMS+Bmp0eNY/63/RPjJ1xvrt5nIHJz6Z6ltsaB3UdCpm3QABPnO4CJzfYqxcVNezydGBO0w7y3RA==`; it was built and published with provenance by [workflow run 39027790810](https://github.com/f4ah6o/dsh-SIWC/actions/runs/39027790810). The local candidate tarball is [`dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz), SHA-256 `7425bc6ed094e2c9e560b9d9700bb204271f7e37fd2a126bfa9c2df08ea10039`; it is an ignored, untracked workspace file. Both the local candidate and the registry artifact passed the build, typecheck, and 75-test suite, the auxiliary wire probe against published DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` packages, and an installed Web smoke on the current `0.2.1-rc.2` runtime, where the Host Remote loaded and the ChatGPT settings section rendered the empty-account state. No live ChatGPT inference was performed for this release. The earlier [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.1`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz) tarball, SHA-256 `3c5f83e28a590c804245d05791b5cbead7fbbcc400649ed861bf775c02524a02`, remains historical. The [alpha artifact comparison](validation/alpha-artifact-proof.json) records that the alpha.1 and `0.1.0` tarballs differ in the three package READMEs, the version-only manifest change, and generated CSS-map property ordering in `lib/client.js`; the CSS maps have the same key/value pairs. Desktop acceptance remains pending. A Windows Desktop attempt with official DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` failed after plugin installation because `ctx.connection` was missing when Desktop read `authenticatedUrl`; the underlying composition cause is unresolved. See the [verification report](validation/fork-verification.md) and [installed-Desktop checklist](validation/desktop-verification.md).

## Validation artifacts

- [Japanese package setup](packages/chatgpt/README.ja.md)
- Prior prepublication candidate: [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0.tgz), ignored and untracked; its SHA-256 is `15c16502dc658f752c5551b116d98dae286f32c69de3cc9e4d54a279ef1c4110`.
- Published alpha: [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@f12o/dsh-siwc/v/0.1.0-alpha.5), registry SHA-256 `9ca8b408d0336423aa02f25a1bdf8df39e67678d6b0dbc7bc153d2152dba3c55`, SHA-1 `f16d3aa8adae1e67183fbbb26d0a4f99b5fce1e2`; build, typecheck, 75 tests, the auxiliary wire probe, and an installed Web smoke passed on DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`.
- Local alpha candidate: [`dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz), SHA-256 `7425bc6ed094e2c9e560b9d9700bb204271f7e37fd2a126bfa9c2df08ea10039`; ignored and untracked, kept as the pre-publication validation artifact.

plugins.description: Independent Auto Review model settings and GUI for DeepSeek Harness.
plugins.readme_text:
# Independent Auto Review

Use a separate model to review DSH tool calls. Keep the main model unchanged.

This project targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.1` and Node 24. It replaces the built-in experimental Auto Review component. It does not replace the main agent or the model adapter. Other DSH versions are not verified.

## Repository and distribution

Public source repository: [QR-0W/dsh-independent-auto-review](https://github.com/QR-0W/dsh-independent-auto-review).

**Version `0.2.1` adapts the bundle to DSH `0.2.1-rc.1`.** The review policy and the separate review route are unchanged; the review evidence now reads the working directory through the Host `workingDirectory` service, and the retained upstream source is re-vendored at `0.2.1-rc.1`. The gate and settings still ship as one installed package. The local profile was migrated, the restarted Host reads the original reviewer configuration, and the user confirmed that the new GUI displays and saves correctly. Minimal pre-write validation and isolated cold migration/restoration tests also pass. The SDK has not been modified and generic automatic rollback is not claimed. See [verification status](docs/gui-verification.md) and [scope](docs/migration-goal.md).

The new package contains two sibling Host components: the review gate and the settings service. The settings service is exported as `@local/dsh-independent-auto-review/settings`; it is not a separate installed package. The root also ships the Client form and its prebuilt artifact. No install-time build script is needed.

The old `@local/dsh-independent-auto-review-settings` companion must not coexist as an active provider with the integrated settings service. Its separate package and patch have been removed from this source, and the old companion is no longer installed in the verified local profile.

## Installation

The verified handoff uses an actual Host restart rather than dependence on generic SDK automatic rollback. Profile changes affect all sessions; obtain permission before stopping another installation's Host.

1. Use a tested, reviewed artifact or commit. Register a valid review model adapter; explicit reasoning effort must be supported.
2. In a development checkout, run `npm run link:runtime` to link the exact shipped APIs. Do not install another runtime or hand-edit the profile.
3. Confirm the current reviewer values. Quiesce saves and have the user select a manual permission mode before the handoff; do not change the main model.
4. Disable the old settings companion through Plugin Manager before activating the integrated settings provider. Keep the built-in gate suppressed. Disabling the entire old root bundle can remove its suppression override; either prove an independently durable override or use an approved stopped-Host update whose first startup retains suppression.
5. Install only the root package through Plugin Manager. Its two Host rows must remain siblings. Check application outcomes and absence of duplicate service, tool or Auto-gate registrations.
6. Refresh the existing GUI and verify **Plugins → Installed → Independent Auto Review** displays and reads the form. Verify reload and changed-value saving with approved temporary values, then restore them.
7. Remove the disabled old companion only after successful new-package validation. Confirm exactly one installed bundle card. Auto selection remains a separate user action.

Do not hand-edit the profile's package manifest or patch. Package and profile changes use the plugin manager. Configuration writes use the public Host configuration service.

The checked-in default is environment-specific:

```yaml
reviewer:
  provider: gptpro
  model: codex-auto-review
  reasoningEffort: medium
  timeoutMs: 60000
```

It is not a bundled model service. Public users must supply a valid registered route. The local `tools/preflight` helper fills missing metadata for this specific route only. It declares local limits of 128000 context tokens and 8192 output tokens, not measured gateway capacities. It preserves other models, provider settings, and credential references. It does not read or store API keys.

## Configure the reviewer

The GUI edits the independent reviewer, not the main model. Only an explicit save writes. The form retains its draft after a failure and uses a revision fence to prevent overwriting concurrent changes.

The core reviewer is not a volatile settings consumer. Saving through the shared ConfigEditor operation uses its normal configuration lifecycle. It reloads the reviewer and can move Auto sessions to confined `workspace-write`. Select Auto again after the new configuration is active. Changing the main-model selection does not reload the reviewer. Saving does not test the gateway or select Auto.

Provider and model identifiers are exact. The GUI does not prove gateway connectivity or backend model identity. An unsupported route or explicit reasoning level stops review; no main-model fallback exists.

An empty GUI reasoning field inherits the bundle's default. If `reasoningEffort` is absent from all configuration layers, the review adapter uses its own default. Timeout must be an integer from 1 to 300000 milliseconds.

The deferred `auto_review_settings` management tool reads and saves through the same Host operation. Use `get` first, then supply that revision as `expectedRevision` with `set`. A stale revision rejects the write. The tool cannot select Auto or approve a pending tool call.

## Safety

- Review native tool calls and PTC inner calls, not the outer `run_code` transport.
- Retain the upstream policy and evidence roles.
- Require a valid decision and a terminal `stop`.
- Deny on review failure. Do not start the tool body.
- Preserve later permission denials and tool guards.
- Under `ask`, a review denial can request manual approval. Under `never`, the denial is final.
- Cancellation cannot grant a pending call.
- Removal cancels active reviews and selects confined `workspace-write` for Auto sessions. Preserve an existing `never` policy.

The adapter must honor abort. Iterator cleanup waits at most one second. A defective adapter can retain network activity after that wait, but cannot grant the pending call.

Model review is probabilistic. Do not use it as the only control for sensitive systems.

**Warning:** The locally configured GPT Pro gateway uses HTTP. Review evidence can contain private project data. That connection has no TLS protection.

## Remove or roll back

The integrated package has no separately installed GUI companion. Disabling its settings Host row withdraws the settings service and tool; disabling the gate withdraws independent review. Whole-bundle disable removes both and can also remove the built-in suppression patch.

For migration rollback, remain in manual mode and withdraw new providers before restoring old artifacts and the complete raw gate override through supported management/configuration APIs. Prove durable built-in suppression or use an approved stopped-Host handoff. Restore the old companion only after the new service/tool is gone. Verify the recovered configuration and single review integration before the user selects Auto. Do not infer safe recovery from a successful install response.

Review-model metadata added during setup remains after removal. It does not affect the main model.

## Development and verification

End users do not need a compiler. For development, rebuild the GUI after editing its source:

```sh
npm run link:runtime
npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/gui/build-tools
npm run build:gui
npm run check
```

Tests use the installed runtime. Set `DSH_RUNTIME_DIR` when DSH is not in the global npm directory. Shared APIs are declared in peer and development dependencies. The linking helper supplies the exact shipped APIs; it does not install another runtime. The compiler dependencies stay in the separate build-tools directory.

The current suite passes 120 tests, including real rejection of invalid identifiers before disk writes or gate reload. The gate implementation is unchanged; its Config schema now matches the existing identifier rules. With `IAR_ROLLBACK_DIR` naming the retained old-artifact dir

plugins.description: Manually resume an interrupted DSH conversation: /continue and an action-row action pick the run up exactly where it stopped.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-continuechat

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Manually resume an interrupted DeepSeek Harness conversation.

When a turn ends early — stopped by hand, cut short by a failed model request, or truncated by the output-token limit — the harness leaves nothing behind but a "stopped" marker. This plugin adds the missing step: a `/continue` command and a **Continue** action in the action row under the interrupted reply itself, so the run picks up exactly where it stopped instead of restarting.

## What it solves

| Situation | Without the plugin | With the plugin |
|---|---|---|
| You hit stop by accident | Retype "continue" yourself | Click **Continue** |
| A network or provider failure aborted the turn | Restate the context before the model resumes | The plugin hands the recorded failure to the model and resumes |
| The reply was cut off by the token limit | The harness says *send "continue"* — with no entry point | One click or one command continues the answer |

## Usage

### Command

```
/continue
/continue also fix the remaining three files
```

Text after the command name is appended to the continuation prompt as an "Additional instruction from the user" line.

The command's outcome (`已请求继续对话（中断原因：手动停止）。`) is rendered by the harness command plane; it never becomes a model message.

### Button

On the turn that was cut short, a **Continue** action appears in the action row under the closing assistant message — the same row that carries copy / thumbs-up / thumbs-down / branch:

- **It only appears on a real interruption.** Turns that completed, were blocked, or merely closed a fork show nothing, so the button never shows up under a conversation that ended normally.
- Only the assistant message that closes that turn carries it; every other message renders nothing and takes no space.
- It disappears again once the agent is running.
- Clicking it is exactly one `/continue` execution.
- A failed attempt keeps a short error line next to the action (hover for the full text).

The decision comes from the session's durable event window: the newest `turn/end` must have a resumable reason *and* that turn must carry a **persistent** assistant message. A turn that was interrupted **before producing any assistant output** (a request that failed outright, a process that died before streaming) therefore has nowhere to host the button — use the `/continue` command there.

### Command menu

Type `/` and pick `continue` ("Continue the interrupted conversation from where it stopped"). Arrow keys plus Enter are enough — no draft typing required.

## How it works

### Interruption tracking (host half)

The plugin subscribes to the session log's `session/event` and tracks every turn end:

| `reason.kind` | Meaning | Resumable |
|---|---|---|
| `aborted` | Run cancelled. `reason.reason.kind` refines it: `user` stopped by hand, `parent` stopped by a parent operation, `hook` stopped by a harness hook, `disposed` session torn down | ✅ |
| `error` | Model request failed (network, auth, server) | ✅ |
| `max-tokens` | Reply truncated by the output-token limit (not a context-window overflow) | ✅ |
| `interrupted` | Turn closed by crash recovery after the host process was interrupted | ✅ |
| `completed` | Finished normally | ❌ |
| `blocked` | Step refused by `agent/pre-step` before entering | ❌ |
| `forked` | Fork seed closing an inherited prefix (the start of a new session) | ❌ |

Any later `user/message` clears the record — either the user took over, or the plugin already resumed the run.

### The continuation prompt

`/continue` does not send a bare "continue". It queues a structured user message:

```
<continue-conversation>
The previous turn ended early: the run was stopped by hand.
Continue the interrupted work in this same session, from exactly where it stopped:
- Do not restart the task, re-summarize, or repeat output and work that is already visible above.
- Treat the current workspace, tool results, and durable session state as authoritative; …
- If a tool call was interrupted, verify its outcome before retrying it, and never blindly retry an operation that may have side effects.
- Finish the remaining work, then verify the result before reporting it.
Failure recorded by the harness: <what the harness logged when the turn died>
Additional instruction from the user: <text typed after the command>
</continue-conversation>
```

The first line is rewritten per reason (stopped by hand / request failed / reply cut off / crash recovery), and the harness-recorded failure text is attached so the model knows *why* the turn ended — which is what decides between continuing to write and re-checking an interrupted tool call first.

### Why the answer is a separate message

After you press **Continue**, DSH opens a new turn for the model to write on, and the plugin then retires that turn's trigger prompt from the transcript — so you no longer see the prompt, and the interrupted reply is followed directly by the new text.

The retirement is a `system/message` replacement, and the log makes such an event *step-scoped*: its `turn`/`step` must name the step that is open as it lands, and both coordinates must be positive (`dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4/lib/index.js`, `assertV4SystemMessageFields` plus the relationship replay). A turn that has already ended names no open step, so the replacement cannot be written there. It rides the step that produced the model's answer to the prompt — or, for a turn that produced none, the next step that opens.

The new text **cannot be merged into the original message**. That is an architectural constraint of the DSH session log, not an implementation shortcut:

- The log is event-sourced: a committed assistant message cannot be edited, only shadowed by a surface `replace`.
- A `replace` must list every shadowed node in `sourceEventSeqs` (`dsh-session/lib/index.js:327`), while `assistant/message` is explicitly forbidden from carrying that field (`:313`, it embeds its provider stream). The two rules conflict, so no assistant event can perform a replacement.
- Shadowing the whole range with a `system/message` instead would also shadow the `tool/call` / `tool/result` pairs inside it, breaking the model history so the next request fails.

The provider side has no assistant prefill either (`dsh-llm-deepseek` carries only anthropic-beta flags), so the model cannot literally continue the previous assistant message — it must generate a new one.

The result: **no stray "continue" prompt, but still a separate new answer.**

### Message shape

The continuation message is built by hand as `{ id, role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text }], source: { kind: 'continue-chat' } }` and frozen:

- **The `id` is mandatory.** `Agent.inbox` deduplicates pending messages by `message.id` (a duplicate throws `already pending`) and never mints one, so the plugin generates it with `randomUUID()` from `node:crypto`.
- **`source.kind` is `continue-chat`.** Chat classifies a `user/message` by its source kind: `user` would render the prompt as a human bubble, while any other kind renders it as an injected-context node — and a context node whose content is plain text stays out of the visible node set. Never use `'plugin'` either: that is only the legacy format-v3 shape and format v4 rejects it when reading a log back.
- As a result the host half imports **nothing but `node:crypto`**: no `peerDependencies`, and therefore no exposure to the plugin version-compatibility gate.

### The browser half

The client half does exactly two things:

1. Registers the `continue-chat` dictionaries (zh/en).
2. Registers one action in the `conversation.chat.assistant-actions` slot. That slot's owner prop is `messageId` and its entries render inside Chat's `MessageIconActions` — the very component that owns copy / rating / branch — so the button lands in that row by construction.

Clicking it runs `ctx.remote.commands.execute(sessionId, '/continue', [])`, the same path a hand-typed `/continue` takes, so command lifecycle records, result rendering, and logging all stay identical.

Whether a message belongs to an interrupted turn is answered by the session's own durable event window: `ctx.s
